aiToday.executiveSummary: Public finances, energy costs and housing dominate today’s supplied coverage. France faces another parliamentary setback over its 2027 budgets, alongside hundreds of planned protest actions on 17 October. Italy has reached a preliminary agreement with the European Commission on energy-bill measures, while funding constraints limit tax-cut ambitions. Portugal is backing joint gas purchasing and stronger European refining capacity, with housing protests and TAP sale negotiations also prominent. Spain combines political fragmentation ahead of the 29 November election with major international motorway wins for Ferrovial and a €315 million investment plan from Cortizo. Luxembourg’s narrower coverage centres on proposed restrictions on settlement imports and a long-delayed residential development.

countryBriefs.summary: MPs have rejected the 2027 social-security budget in committee, following rejection of the state budget there. This is a political setback rather than a direct procedural block: the original social-security text goes to the chamber from Tuesday. Libération links France’s high borrowing costs to political and parliamentary uncertainty. Hundreds of protest actions are planned for 17 October, with disturbances expected. Anti-poverty organisations are also challenging proposed spending cuts. Infrastructure coverage includes the inauguration of the Recyti sorting centre at Vaux-le-Pénil and redevelopment of Place Anatole-France in Vigneux-sur-Seine.

Ferrovial has won Atlanta’s I-285 East motorway auction, following wins on Tennessee’s I-24 and the Czech D35. Cortizo plans to invest €315 million through 2030 to support international growth. Ahead of the 29 November election, alliances to the left of the PSOE remain fragmented, although IU has joined the Compromís-Podemos pact in Valencia. Irene Montero won Podemos’s uncontested primary amid sharply lower participation. PSOE spokesperson Montse Mínguez has resigned after reporting on her partner’s property businesses. Sánchez also faces European criticism over migrant regularisation.

The government has reached a preliminary agreement with the European Commission on its energy-bills decree, moving towards approval of a gas-price cap while leaving emissions-trading measures outside the package. Budget room remains tight: reporting says the proposed middle-income tax cut lacks funding, while Economy Minister Giorgetti is pressing banks to contribute and describing competing relief measures as alternatives. The government has also approved a commissioner structure for the third pillar of its housing plan. In Candela, farmers and hauliers have mounted a road blockade against rising costs.

Montenegro supports joint gas purchasing and stronger European refining capacity as Brussels examines a collective response to rising gas prices. Housing remains politically contentious after Porto protests; the prime minister expressed concern over threats against his home, while Castro Almeida urged local authorities to help address the housing problem. Jornal de Negócios reports that the government is seeking up to €30 million from Lufthansa to seal the TAP sale. Parliament has approved parental leave paid at 100% for up to six months from 2027. Grilo Tunnel works will restrict traffic from Monday.

The government has examined a text establishing a legal framework to prohibit imports of goods from Israeli settlements in occupied Palestinian territories. Foreign Minister Xavier Bettel says the initiative concerns respect for international law rather than opposition to Israel. In construction, RTL reports that the Belair residential complex in Dudelange remains unfinished nearly six years after one buyer purchased an apartment off-plan. Today’s supplied coverage of Luxembourg’s economy and infrastructure is otherwise limited, with no broader construction figures or major investment announcements provided.
